findings.title: Obot MCP platform published multiple access-control and SSRF CVEs

visible_dates.date_type: published and lastModified timestamps for CVE-2026-101062, CVE-2026-101063, CVE-2026-101064, CVE-2026-101065, and CVE-2026-101084

findings.evidence_classification: Primary vulnerability database records with linked project and VulnCheck advisories
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Obot before v0.23.0 for OAuth registration, registry authentication, and remote MCP SSRF; before v0.21.1 for /mcp-connect access-control bypass; Docker quickstart through commit d7e6970 documented unauthenticated 0.0.0.0:8080 deployment with /var/run/docker.sock mounted.
findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD records published on 2026-09-27 describe Obot flaws allowing attacker OAuth client registration and token misuse, unauthenticated MCP Registry metadata reads, SSRF through remote MCP server registration, unauthenticated administrative access from the Docker quickstart, and bypass of Access Control Rules on /mcp-connect.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Obot is an AI agent/MCP platform, so these issues directly affect delegated authority, MCP server registration, OAuth scoping, registry exposure, and host control-plane safety for agent systems.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki_note: Obot as a broad AI agent/MCP platform entity belongs upstream if a durable product/framework page is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki_note: General deployment practice and agent workflow governance should route to ai-dev-wiki; this repo should keep the authentication, MCP, SSRF, and Docker-socket risk analysis.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence on dates and security content because the NVD API returned exact in-window timestamps and concrete vulnerability descriptions. Follow linked GitHub/VulnCheck pages during ingest for fixed-version wording and advisory identifiers.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, split into local leaves for Obot MCP OAuth token scoping, registry authentication, remote MCP SSRF, quickstart unauthenticated admin exposure, and /mcp-connect access-control bypass if each remains independently useful.
Check whether upstream ai-wiki already owns Obot as an entity before creating local navigation text.
Verify final fixed versions and whether docker-socket exposure is documentation-only or has runtime guardrails.

findings.title: Heym LLM and MCP workflow CVEs covered SSRF and plaintext capability secrets

visible_dates.date_type: published and lastModified timestamps for CVE-2026-100858, CVE-2026-100862, and CVE-2026-100863

findings.evidence_classification: Primary vulnerability database records with linked GitHub and VulnCheck advisories
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: heym before 0.0.109 for Slack, Discord, and Crawler workflow-node SSRF; heym before 0.0.91 for LLM image-edit SSRF/IP validation and plaintext capability secret handling.
findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD records published on 2026-09-27 describe Heym SSRF gaps in Slack, Discord, Crawler, and LLM image-edit workflow paths, plus plaintext storage or return of capability secrets including MCP API keys, webhook auth values, portal session tokens, workflow execution JWTs, Discord interaction tokens, and global variables.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Workflow systems that connect LLM, MCP, webhook, and crawler nodes need egress controls and secret handling that survive user-authored workflows; these CVEs expose cloud metadata/internal services and reusable agent capability credentials.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki_note: Heym as a workflow automation/AI integration product can route upstream if durable product coverage is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki_note: General workflow-authoring and automation patterns route to ai-dev-wiki; this repo should retain SSRF, MCP API key, and workflow-secret controls.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence on in-window dates and affected versions from NVD. Ingest should refetch GitHub advisories because the linked pages may contain clearer patched-version and mitigation wording than the API snippets.
follow_up_actions: Create or update local leaves for workflow-node SSRF guard bypasses, LLM image-fetch egress validation, and MCP/workflow capability secret handling.

findings.title: UTCP MCP and HTTP plugins published tool URL validation CVEs

visible_dates.date_type: published and lastModified timestamps for CVE-2026-101057 and CVE-2026-101058

findings.affected_boundary_or_version: utcp-mcp through 1.1.2 fixed in 1.1.3; python-utcp package utcp-http before 1.1.12 fixed in 1.1.12.
findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD records published on 2026-09-27 describe utcp-mcp dialing configured MCP server URLs without the same secure URL validation used by HTTP-family plugins, and utcp-http accepting remote manuals that declare loopback tool URLs, enabling loopback SSRF when a victim registers an attacker-served manual.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Tool-calling protocols need strict URL provenance and loopback handling because remote manuals and MCP server configurations become delegated tool authority inside agent clients.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki_note: UTCP as a tool-calling protocol/entity belongs upstream if durable ecosystem coverage is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki_note: General tool-calling implementation practice routes to ai-dev-wiki; this repo should retain SSRF, cleartext MCP connection, and local-loopback policy implications.

findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence. NVD provides exact dates and concrete affected versions, but no GitHub advisory URL was captured in the quick API evidence; ingest should enrich references.
follow_up_actions: Refetch CVE detail records for linked references before durable synthesis.
Compare UTCP URL-validation lessons with existing MCP URL, OAuth, and SSRF leaves.
Route broad UTCP protocol context upstream if it is not already represented.

findings.title: Penpot MCP server plugin WebSocket bridge lacked authentication in single-user mode

visible_dates.date_type: published and lastModified timestamp for CVE-2026-100868

findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD records published on 2026-09-27 describe Penpot before 2.18.0 binding the MCP server plugin WebSocket bridge to all network interfaces without authentication in single-user mode, allowing adjacent-network attackers to impersonate the browser plugin, intercept task payloads, and forge results returned to the MCP client.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP bridges that connect desktop or browser plugins to design tools become agent trust boundaries; unauthenticated network listeners can compromise tool outputs and task payload integrity.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki_note: Penpot as a product/entity belongs upstream if general product coverage is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki_note: General plugin bridge design may route to ai-dev-wiki; this repo owns MCP bridge authentication and task-output integrity implications.

findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence from exact NVD timestamp and concrete affected version. Ingest should enrich with vendor release or advisory links.
follow_up_actions: Refetch CVE detail for references and fixed-release evidence.
Consider a local leaf for MCP WebSocket bridge listener authentication if similar bridge issues recur.
